clue.text: Giant cuts after two clubs squeeze pay finally

indicators.note: after places the cutting word behind the club-and-pay group
the two club letters squeeze something between them, so they hold it inside

parts.note: C is the card abbreviation for clubs, so two of them give C and C

indicators.note: finally asks for the closing letter of the word pay

parts.note: lops means cuts, as of branches

explanation.surface: A giant takes cuts to his pay once two clubs put the squeeze on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'squeeze' puts Y, the last letter of 'pay', between the two Cs; 'after' then places LOPS behind.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cyclopes of Greek myth were one-eyed giants, so one of them is an example of a giant.

clue.text: One-time consul about to chill half of Rome

parts.note: C is circa, Latin for about
to ice is to chill

indicators.note: half of takes the first two letters of the four-letter city name

explanation.surface: A former consul is about to cool down half of Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of' gives RO from Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: Marcus Tullius Cicero served as a consul of the Roman Republic in 63 BC.

clue.text: Cargo ship unable to avoid contact with mine

definitions.text: Cargo ship unable to avoid contact with mine

parts.words: Cargo ship unable to avoid contact with mine
parts.note: reads like a ship about to hit a sea mine, but it describes a vessel whose freight always comes from a coal pit

explanation.definitionFit: A collier is a ship built to carry coal, which is dug from a mine.

clue.text: Unfair one particular song's not being broadcast

parts.note: a bit off means unfair or unacceptable
the definite article picks out one particular thing
an air is a song or tune

explanation.surface: It is unfair that one particular song is not getting played on the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' in its sense of not on, 'a bit off', means unfair.
explanation.definitionFit: A programme that has stopped transmission is no longer on radio or television.

clue.text: One who may have done coping with a successful dieter?

definitions.text: One who may have done coping

explanation.surface: Someone who has coped may be a dieter who has done well.
explanation.walkthrough: Coping is the capping course on a wall, done by a mason; a dieter who loses stones (14-pound units) is a stone cutter.
explanation.definitionFit: A mason who shapes stone may have made a wall's coping, while one who sheds stones of weight cuts them.

clue.text: Old book illustration: here are two examples as plan can show

parts.note: as and plan stand for ash and plane, two trees and so two examples of timber
as and plan show those tree names with their final letters lopped, so they display a cut

explanation.surface: A caption explains that an old book illustration shows two examples of what a plan can show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'here are' only links. 'as' and 'plan' are ash and plane, each with its last letter cut off: two woods, each cut, so the clue's own words display the reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A print made from a carved block of timber was the standard way to illustrate early printed books.

clue.text: Intelligence having to abandon lead in Helmand

indicators.note: to abandon says the following letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: with means having, as in a man with money

indicators.note: lead in takes the leading letter of Helmand

explanation.surface: Intelligence officers have to leave their lead role in Helmand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to abandon' takes H, the first of 'Helmand', out of WITH.
explanation.definitionFit: Wit can mean mental sharpness or intelligence, as in having one's wits about one.

clue.text: I'm found at the bar — a habitual response after work

indicators.note: after places the response word behind the work word

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work
a tic is an involuntary habitual twitch

explanation.surface: A drinker turns up at the bar as a matter of habit after finishing work.
explanation.walkthrough: In a British pub an optic is the measuring dispenser fixed to an upturned spirits bottle behind the bar.
explanation.definitionFit: The measuring device on spirits bottles hangs behind a pub's counter, so it is found at the bar.

clue.text: My air conditioning is set up for a Mediterranean location

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like my!

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means the words are raised, so read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone's air conditioning has been installed for a Mediterranean holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns AC + IS into SICA.
explanation.definitionFit: Corsica is a French island in the Mediterranean Sea.

clue.text: Sickness which drivers must watch out for on high mountain roads?

definitions.text: which drivers must watch out for on high mountain roads?

explanation.surface: An illness that motorists must look out for on alpine roads.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is decompression sickness in divers.
explanation.definitionFit: Decompression sickness is the bends, and mountain roads are full of sharp curves.

clue.text: Conservative finds former confidence which might change the weather

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative, the British political party
old means former, as in an old flame
front means boldness or nerve, as in having the front to do something

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician recovers an earlier self-assurance that might shift the political climate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confidence' is front in the sense of cheek, not the weather sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The leading edge of an advancing mass of cool air brings a shift in meteorological conditions, often rain.

clue.text: Abrupt aspect of quartermaster sergeant

indicators.note: aspect of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Curtness is one side of the quartermaster sergeant's character.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe speech that is short and brusque to the point of rudeness.

clue.text: One put in charge of the BBC and their broadcast

definitions.text: One put in charge of the BBC

indicators.note: broadcast in its sense of scattered widely signals the letters of their being spread into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone appointed to run the BBC and its programmes.
explanation.walkthrough: John Reith was the first Director-General of the BBC, the British public broadcaster.
explanation.definitionFit: John Reith headed the British Broadcasting Corporation as its founding general manager and Director-General.

clue.text: Striking operative producing the desired result

explanation.surface: A worker on strike nonetheless gets the outcome they wanted.
explanation.walkthrough: A triple definition: 'Striking' (impressive), 'operative' (in force), and 'producing the desired result'.
explanation.definitionFit: Effective means impressive in look, in force as a rule, and successful in achieving its purpose.

clue.text: Stir with English felon suffering without a penny?

definitions.text: Stir with English felon suffering without a penny?

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the jumbled letters go around the penny
suffering says the letters are in a bad way, so they are rearranged

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for penny

explanation.surface: A penniless English criminal is sent to suffer in jail.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a whole-clue definition too: the Fleet was a London prison used mostly for debtors, which suits a penniless felon.
explanation.definitionFit: The Fleet was a historic London jail largely used for debtors, so stir for the penniless.

clue.text: Love one's estate to produce good yarn

parts.note: treasure is a term of endearment, like love
one's read as one is gives I and S
land is an estate, a landed property

explanation.surface: Someone tells their darling that their property will make a fine woollen yarn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's' is read as 'one is', giving I + S. The good yarn is Stevenson's pirate story.
explanation.definitionFit: Stevenson's pirate adventure is a classic gripping tale, and a yarn is a story.

clue.text: System of communication from coast fixing east on chart

indicators.note: fixing means the coast word has the other pieces fixed inside it

parts.note: shore means coast

indicators.note: on in a down clue puts the first letter above the chart word

parts.note: a map is a chart

explanation.surface: A signalling system from the coast fixes an eastern position on a chart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' only links the definition to the wordplay; in a down clue 'on' stacks east above chart.
explanation.definitionFit: Semaphore is a signalling method using flags or arms in set positions to send messages.

clue.text: Queen is about to annoy husband with odd behaviour

indicators.note: about means the queen and is pieces wrap around the annoy word

parts.note: taken as written
to irk is to annoy

explanation.surface: A queen is about to irritate her husband with her strange conduct.
explanation.walkthrough: QU for queen is a crossword shorthand; the definition is adjectival, describing someone marked by odd behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Quirkish means having quirks, so marked by peculiar habits.

clue.text: Men rate student abysmally and that's putting it mildly

indicators.note: abysmally says the letters perform terribly, so they are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Men give a student a terrible rating, and that is saying it gently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abysmally' rearranges all fourteen letters of 'Men rate student'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is said when a remark plays something down, exactly what an understated comment does.

clue.text: What one might do to plot a line using computer technology

parts.words: What one might do to plot
parts.note: you dig a garden plot, so you might dig it

explanation.surface: Someone asks what to do to plot a graph line with a computer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plot' is a patch of land, not a graph: you dig it.
explanation.definitionFit: Digital describes technology that works with data as numbers, as computers do.

clue.text: Hot flan needs cooking thoroughly

indicators.note: cooking means the letters are being worked on, so they come out rearranged

explanation.surface: A hot flan needs to be cooked all the way through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs' only links; 'cooking' rearranges HOT FLAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The British phrase is a strong yes, meaning very much or to the fullest extent.

clue.text: Beware going over lines s-I was shot by the Germans

definitions.text: I was shot by the Germans

indicators.note: going over in a down clue puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: cave is old schoolboy slang from Latin for look out or beware
L is the abbreviation for line, so two give lines

explanation.surface: A warning to watch out when crossing lines, from a speaker shot by German soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: Edith Cavell was a British nurse executed by a German firing squad in 1915.
explanation.definitionFit: The British nurse Edith Cavell was shot by German forces in occupied Belgium in 1915.

clue.text: Doctor getting essence right in back case

indicators.note: the back word acts as a case holding the other letters inside it

parts.note: rear means back
gist means essence, the main point

explanation.surface: A doctor gets the essence of a case right while in the back.
explanation.walkthrough: A registrar is a British hospital doctor grade, below consultant; 'Doctor' does not signal an anagram here.
explanation.definitionFit: In British hospitals a registrar is a grade of doctor training as a specialist below consultant.

clue.text: Where one may replace clothes son's ripped

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son
tore means ripped

explanation.surface: Somewhere to replace clothes because a son has torn them.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop is where one buys things, including new clothes to replace old ones.

clue.text: Picturesque city depicted by favourite artist

parts.note: a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet
RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist

explanation.surface: A scenic city is shown in a painting by someone's favoured artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depicted by' only links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient rock-cut city in Jordan is famous for its striking rose-red facades.

clue.text: Where King Priam came to an end, not finishing overture

parts.note: in names a place, the where of the phrase

indicators.note: not finishing says the final letter of the phrase is dropped

parts.words: King Priam came to an end
parts.note: Priam, king of Troy in Greek legend, was killed when his city fell

explanation.surface: An opera about King Priam's death is played without completing its overture.
explanation.walkthrough: King Priam is also a Tippett opera, which sets up the musical surface; 'not finishing' drops the Y.
explanation.definitionFit: An introduction to a musical piece is its opening section, and an overture opens an opera.

clue.text: What may feature actors no longer capable of spoken English

parts.note: past means no longer current
oral means spoken

explanation.surface: A production whose actors can no longer speak English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capable of' only links the pieces; a pastorale is usually music, but it can also be a staged rural play.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastorale can be a dramatic piece on a rustic theme, so performers may appear in one.

clue.text: God the father by name

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for father

explanation.surface: A god is the father in name only.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' only links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Pan is the Greek god of shepherds and the wild.

clue.text: Court painter's predicament involving bishop at residence

indicators.note: involving means the predicament word wraps around the bishop letter

parts.note: being in a hole is being in a predicament
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
in means at home, as in staying in

explanation.surface: A royal painter finds himself in trouble with a bishop at his home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involving' puts B inside HOLE to give HOLBE.
explanation.definitionFit: Hans Holbein the Younger was the official painter at the court of Henry VIII.

clue.text: Paying attention's new for husband, but indispensable

indicators.note: new for husband means the husband letter is swapped out for the new letter

parts.note: heedful means paying attention

explanation.surface: Being attentive is new behaviour for a husband, but it is essential.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new for husband' replaces H with N.
explanation.definitionFit: Needful means required or necessary, so a thing that cannot be done without.
